#Module performance

High Resolution Time and User Timing: performance.now() and timeOrigin on the page's own timeline, mark / measure, getEntriesByName / getEntriesByType (one entry at a time), clearMarks / clearMeasures. Entries are kept in startTime order, at most performance.max_user_timing_entries (the oldest go first).

Exposed to: Window, Worker. Source: api/performance.widl.

#Types

#enum PerformanceEntryType : i32

The entries a query matches (Any: every user timing entry). The values from Navigation on are the browser's timeline entries (Performance_timeline): the document's navigation, its resources, paints, slow inputs and long tasks (Long_Task: a task of the window's realm that took 50 ms or more), the largest contentful paint, the layout shifts, the element timing entries and the visibility-state changes.

membervalue

Mark1

Long_Animation_Frame13
Script14

#callback TimelineCallback

void TimelineCallback(i32 user, i32 kinds)

A function of the realm the browser calls when a kind of timeline entry it was asked for (Performance_timelineInterest) has new entries: kinds has one bit for each (1 << PerformanceEntryType).

#Performance_timeline

string Performance_timeline(PerformanceEntryType entry_type, u64 from_seq = 0)

The timeline entries of entry_type (Navigation, Resource, Paint, Event or First_Input) whose sequence number is at least from_seq, in order, as a JSON array of objects with the members of the entry's interface (name, startTime, duration, initiatorType, responseStart...) and seq. A kept entry never changes; the buffers drop their oldest entries (performance.resource_timing_entries...).

Host: Performance_timeline :: proc(c: ^Call, entry_type: Api_PerformanceEntryType, from_seq: u64) -> string

#Performance_timelineNextSeq

u64 Performance_timelineNextSeq(PerformanceEntryType entry_type)

The sequence number the next entry of this kind will have.

Host: Performance_timelineNextSeq :: proc(c: ^Call, entry_type: Api_PerformanceEntryType) -> u64

#Performance_timelineNode

u64 Performance_timelineNode(PerformanceEntryType entry_type, u64 seq, u32 index)

Wraps the DOM node a timeline entry refers to and returns its handle, or 0 when there is none or it is no longer in the document: the element of the index-th member of entry seq of entry_type — for Largest_Contentful_Paint and Element, index 0 is the entry's own element (its element attribute); for Layout_Shift, index i is the node of its i-th source (LayoutShiftAttribution.node). The engine carries the other members of each entry in the JSON of Performance_timeline; only live node handles come from here (a handle cannot be put in JSON and stay valid).

Host: Performance_timelineNode :: proc(c: ^Call, entry_type: Api_PerformanceEntryType, seq: u64, index: u32) -> u64

#Performance_timelineInterest

void Performance_timelineInterest(u32 kinds)

The kinds (bits 1 << PerformanceEntryType) a PerformanceObserver wants to hear of: only those wake the realm.

Host: Performance_timelineInterest :: proc(c: ^Call, kinds: u32)

#Performance_onTimeline

void Performance_onTimeline(TimelineCallback callback, i32 user = 0)

Where the browser announces new entries of the kinds of Performance_timelineInterest (a task of the page).

Host: Performance_onTimeline :: proc(c: ^Call, callback: u32, user: i32)

#Performance_setResourceTimingBufferSize

void Performance_setResourceTimingBufferSize(u32 entries)

performance.setResourceTimingBufferSize(n) / performance.clearResourceTimings().

Host: Performance_setResourceTimingBufferSize :: proc(c: ^Call, entries: u32)

#Performance_clearResourceTimings

void Performance_clearResourceTimings()

Host: Performance_clearResourceTimings :: proc(c: ^Call)

#Performance_timingOf

f64 Performance_timingOf(i32 which)

performance.timing (Navigation Timing 1): the moment of attribute which of PerformanceTiming (0 navigationStart, 1 unloadEventStart ... 20 loadEventEnd, in the interface's order) on the page's timeline (ms since the time origin), or NaN when it has not happened or does not apply (the attribute is then 0). The network phases of the document's own fetch are not measured: they are all the time origin.

Host: Performance_timingOf :: proc(c: ^Call, which: i32) -> f64
